To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the growth of pure Fe nanocrystals can be initiated on ultra-thin oxide films on Si(001) by exposure to Fe(C(5)O)(5), that the growth can be enhanced by irradiation of the surface with a low-energy electron beam and that the active centers for initial dissociation are oxygen-containing SiO sites.
the formation of Fe nanocrystals on SiO(x) can be controlled in situ by the electron beam.

(i) the nucleation of pure Fe nanocrystals on SiO(x) is driven by the formation of active sites on the surface, (ii) the density of the nanocrystals can be tuned via the electron irradiation of the SiO(x) surface prior to Fe(CO)5 exposure, and (iii) the growth of the nanocrystal size is limited by the diffusion of Fe atoms on the surface.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of pure iron nanoparticles on SiO(x) surfaces.
a novel method for producing pure Fe nanocrystals in the size range of 10 to 100 nm on SiO(x)/Si(001).
the controlled synthesis of metal nanocrystals on oxide substrates.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the growth of Fe clusters on SiO(x)/Si(001) is driven by the autocatalytic reaction of Fe(CO)5 at the surface of the growing Fe clusters.
this work demonstrates that clean iron nanocrystal growth on SiO(x)/Si(001) is possible under mild conditions, and that the density can be tuned by electron irradiation.
the formation of the iron nanoclusters can be controlled by the preparation of the substrate surface.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have demonstrated that the SiO(x)/Si(001) surface can act as an efficient catalyst for the decomposition of Fe(CCO)(5) and that the density of the Fe nanocrystals can be tuned by the electron irradiation prior to exposure.

the formation of the active sites is a result of the combination of electron irradiation, oxygen desorption, and the presence of SiO(x) on Si(100) substrates, which are the key factors in the generation of the clean Fe nanocrystals.
the SiOx surface can be used as a substrate for the synthesis of pure Fe nanocrystals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of an ultra-thin oxide layer on Si(001) as a support is crucial for the formation of pure Fe nanocrystals.
the use of an ultra-thin oxide film as a precursor to the formation of metal nanoclusters can be a viable approach to generate clean, well-defined metal clusters on a semiconductor surface.

clean iron nanocrystal formation is possible under UHV conditions on a well-defined surface, which can be used for the fabrication of nanostructured magnetic materials. © The Royal Society of Chemistry 2014.
